methods.description: Choose observation for information that can be watched/count immediately, or a survey for information that must be asked; record what the collection task actually asks about.
Record each result once beside its matching category or numerical answer; write/update crossed groups of five and count them to give frequencies, including a zero-valued answer as an actual result.

Combine counts of different people/results by matching category; compare the recorded total with the actual number collected, check notes to correct a known duplicate/omission and avoid guessing a category or inferring all causes from a net difference.

The complete insect-count example supports choosing observation; the survey-preference example supports asking for categories. The temperature example is retained as original context but does not widen this skill into continuous measurement, graphs or later classification terminology.

Keep student language to observing, asking, results, categories, counts and tallies; no nominal/ordinal, qualitative/quantitative, experiment, inference, formal sampling or advanced classification lesson is added. A filled original Stage3 collection booklet was not supplied; numerical tally setout below is honestly indirect.

Prerequisite survey design and earliest Stage3 scope suffice. Checked every24dependent solution:all parts/units/categories/known duplicate/unknown discrepancy are coherent with the revised second step,no artificial repetitive fullTheory labels. Every current mapped item follows its actual stated method; no missing higher-stage method, superficial quota or copied practice example is used. New zero/group-five/count-total and known-error contrasts are structural,not incidental shortcuts; existing valid values need no aesthetic rewrite.

Images4/5 show elementary numeric tallies includingzero and check40values; images6/7 show37values and grouped frequencies. No separate KeyIdeasbox is claimed.
